Mandela Institute MINDS Scholarship Details

The MINDS Scholarship Programme for Leadership Development in Africa was successfully launched in 2017, bringing to realisation our vision of developing young leaders who have a continent-wide development mindset and leaders who can facilitate greater cooperation between African countries.

The Mandela Institute Scholarship 2026 Programme enables African students to study in an African country other than their home country and in this way immerse themselves in richness and diversity that the country and its communities has to offer.

By broadening access to  education, we see the expansion of openness to ideas and the creation of a network of like-minded leaders who will help promote the performance and tangible progress of our continent. 

Mandela Institute Scholarship 2026 Requirements

To be considered for a Mandela Institute Scholarship 2026, applicants must meet the following criteria:

  • Be a national of an African country, residing within the continent.

  • Have been formally accepted by one or more MINDS preferred institution/s outside of your country of citizenship and/ or residency

  • Have been formally accepted by one or more MINDS preferred institution/s to pursue postgraduate studies within the following year

  • Attain a minimum of 70% in each subject/course in the last two completed years of study.

  • Demonstrate leadership abilities or potential, responding to specified questions in the application form.

  • Submit a comprehensive online application with the required supporting documents.

MINDS Scholarships Benefits

The MINDS scholarship covers various expenses, depending on whether it’s a partial or full scholarship. It includes:

  • Tuition fees.

  • Accommodation and meals.

  • One return ticket per duration of studies.

  • A fixed stipend to support living expenses.

Duration of Scholarship

MINDS scholarships apply to full-time studies for a one or two-year Honors or Master’s degree at MINDS preferred institutions. The list of these institutions can be found on the official program webpage.

Required Documents for Nelson Mandela Institute Scholarship 2026

While applying for the 2026 Nelson Mandela Institute Scholarship 2026, you will be required to submit the following documents;

  • A copy of the data/ bio page of your passport.

  • A certified academic transcript/ results slip of the last two years of study.

  • A copy of the official acceptance letter from the university. The letter must:

    • Be addressed to the applicant.

    • State the degree to which the applicant has been accepted to study.

    • State the academic year in which the degree will commence.

    • State the duration of the course (e.g., one year).

  • A copy of a valid study permit or visa, OR proof of application. (Optional)

  • A detailed CV/ Resume of not more than four (4) single-sided pages.

  • Two reference letters (of not more than 3 pages each) addressing the applicant’s demonstration of integrity, their competency and/or potential as a leader, and their commitment to the development of the African continent.

How To Apply for Mandela Institute MINDS Scholarship 2026

Follow these steps to kickstart your leadership journey with Mandela Institute MINDS Scholarship Program:

  1. Visit the MINDS scholarship webpage for detailed insights.

  2. Click on the provided link to submit your application.

  3. Prepare scanned copies of necessary documents in PDF format.

  4. Upload documents, including passport, academic transcripts, acceptance letter, study permit, CV, and reference letters.
